A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Energy Matching work. All 19 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation results, controlled inpainting examples, protein-design experiments, LID estimates and sampling ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised CIFAR-10 generation results and sampling-ablation curves.

M1.justification: Section 2.1.1 and Algorithm 1 change flow-loss time sampling from U(0,1) to U(0,τ*), typically retaining τ*=1 during warm-up. Algorithm 2 makes maximum temperature for data-initialized negatives optional; Appendix D specifies the shared noise/data temperature schedule for CIFAR-10. These refine the training procedure while retaining the architecture and two-objective framework.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic transport example, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet32 generation, CelebA inpainting, AAV medium/hard protein design, and MNIST/CIFAR-10 LID estimation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1, 3 and 6 retain their comparator membership. DDPM and OT-CFM receive updated CIFAR-10 scores, but neither represents a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix D substantially revises the principal image-generation training configurations. CIFAR-10 warm-up/main training changes from 200k/10k to 145k/2k iterations, while Table 1's sampling setup increases from 300 to 325 steps. ImageNet main training changes from 7k to 5k iterations. Both switch τ* from 0.9 to 1.0, alongside learning-rate and other optimization changes. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2/Figure 6 replaces the plotted evidence for the existing CIFAR-10 analysis of sampling time, OT-only versus joint training, and temperature-switch timing. The questions tested remain the same; other energy-landscape, controlled-generation and LID analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same fitness standard-deviation reporting. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; the revised FID results retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Energy Matching FID from 3.97 to 3.34, reproduced DDPM from 6.54 to 6.45, and reproduced OT-CFM from 4.11 to 4.04. Figure 6 revises all three curves, with late-time results now favoring τ*=1.0 over 0.9. These accompany changed settings and do not establish same-setting gains. Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the equilibrium relation from εmax∇logρeq=∇Vθ to εmax∇logρeq=−∇Vθ, making it consistent with the stated Boltzmann density. The remaining theoretical development, including Appendix C's LID derivation, is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about a time-independent scalar potential, generation quality, controlled sampling and LID estimation. Section 3.1 refines '50%' to 'more than 50%' without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of transport versus equilibrium behavior, OT-only sampling deterioration, diversity control and Hessian-based LID estimation remain unchanged. The limitations concerning additional gradient-computation memory and full-Hessian scalability are also retained.

D1.justification: The introductory footnote replaces a promise to release code upon acceptance with a concrete repository address. Appendix D updates existing hyperparameters and explicitly describes CIFAR-10 negative-sample temperature scheduling. Architecture and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to EBMs, flow matching, diffusion models and LID estimators are unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to algorithm comments, the code footnote, the Figure 6 caption, the performance sentence and version/date text. The narrative, section ordering and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redrawn, including changing the blue series markers from squares to circles, and its caption clarifies that τ* varies during sampling. Table 1's caption and some local text layout change. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The corrected equilibrium equation removes a mathematical inconsistency, while the repository pointer and more explicit algorithm settings improve reproducibility information. Updated CIFAR-10 results accompany shorter reported training but more sampling steps and other setting changes, so lower FID alone does not establish a controlled methodological improvement. The gains in correctness and documentation are useful but limited; coverage and most validation remain unchanged.
